title: Add the transport-neutral bee herding pane verb group over a CockpitTransport trait
action: Per D2, one vocabulary for the cockpit. Create `herding/pane_verbs.rs` (declare `pub(crate) mod pane_verbs;` in herding.rs) and route these names in herding.rs's `try_native` match (anchor `"herdr-pane-id" => Some(herdr_pane_id(rest)),`): `pane` (subverbs `current`, `list`, `split`, `run`, `send-text`, `read`, `rename`, `close`, `layout`, `tab-create`, `tab-list`, `tab-focus`), `agent-start`, `pane-id` (`--label <l>`), and `result` (`<dotted.path>`, a transport-neutral twin of `herdr-result` that reads the pane verbs' own envelope). Keep `herdr-result` and `herdr-pane-id` working as-is. Add the names to `router.rs`'s names index beside the existing `herding herdr-pane-id --label <label>` line (anchor `rg -n "herding herdr-pane-id" packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/router.rs`). The trait: in run.rs, make `struct RealHerdr` `pub(crate)` and keep `PaneTransport` untouched; in pane_verbs.rs define `pub(crate) trait CockpitTransport: PaneTransport { fn pane_send_text(&self, pane: &str, text: &str) -> Result<(), String>; fn pane_rename(&self, pane: &str, label: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String>; fn pane_list(&self, workspace: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<PaneRow>, String>; fn tab_list(&self, workspace: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<TabRow>, String>; fn tab_focus(&self, tab: &str) -> Result<(), String>; fn pane_id_by_label(&self, label: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, String> }` with `PaneRow { id, label: Option<String>, tab, cwd: Option<String>, command: Option<String> }` and `TabRow { id, label }`, and implement it for BOTH `RealHerdr` (herdr verbs: `pane send-text <id> <text>`, `pane rename <id> <label>` / `--clear`, `pane list [--workspace <ws>]` parsed from herdr's JSON, `tab list`, `tab focus <id>`) and `RealTmux` (cockpit D3 mapping; the two-call send discipline is tmux-herding-transport's, see its CONTEXT 'Specific Ideas': `send-keys -t <pane> -l <text>` + separate Enter; `select-pane -t <pane> -T <label>` (empty title to clear); `list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}\t#{pane_title}\t#{window_id}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_current_command}'` filtered to the current session when workspace is None; `list-windows -F '#{window_id}\t#{window_name}'`; `select-window -t <id>`; label lookup = first pane whose title equals the label). The phase-1 PaneTransport ops back the rest: `current`→pane_current, `split`→pane_split (flags `--direction right|down --ratio <r> --cwd <dir>`), `run`→pane_run, `read`→pane_read (`--lines N` trims the tail), `close`→pane_close, `layout`→pane_layout, `tab-create`→tab_create (`--label`, `--cwd`, `--workspace` optional: when absent, on herdr resolve the workspace id from `pane_current`'s envelope (herdr `pane current --current` carries `workspace_id`) and refuse with code `workspace_required` if it cannot; on tmux pass the empty string — RealTmux::tab_create ignores it (D3)), `agent-start`→agent_start (`<job> --kind <k> --pane <id> -- <args…>`). Selection: reuse run.rs's `transport_for_run(main_root)` style — expose a `pub(crate) fn cockpit_transport_for(main_root: &Path) -> Result<Box<dyn CockpitTransport>, String>` (Box<dyn CockpitTransport> is fine here; RealHerdr/RealTmux both implement it), with `--main-root` optional on every verb (default `super::resolve_main_root`). Output: EVERY verb prints one JSON envelope `{"ok":true,"transport":"herdr|tmux","result":{…}}` on success (result keys: `current`→`{pane_id, tab_id?, workspace_id?}`; `list`→`{panes:[PaneRow…]}`; `split`/`tab-create`→`{pane_id}`; `tab-list`→`{tabs:[…]}`; `pane-id`→`{pane_id}` or a non-zero `{ok:false,error:{code:"not_found",…}}`; `read`→`{text}`; the rest `{}`), and `{"ok":false,"transport":…,"error":{"code","message"}}` with exit 1 on failure; `bee herding result <dotted.path>` reads such an envelope on stdin and prints the value at `result.<path>` exactly the way `herdr_result` does for herdr bodies (read `fn herdr_result` at herding.rs ~854 and share its path walker). Tests in-module (prefixed `pane_verbs_`): a `FakeCockpit` implementing both traits records calls; each subverb maps its flags to the right trait call and renders the pinned envelope keys; `pane-id` not-found exits 1 with code `not_found`; `result` walks `result.pane_id`. Do NOT edit tmux.rs (thc-2 owns it concurrently) and do not reach its private test stub: put the `impl CockpitTransport for RealTmux` block in pane_verbs.rs (a crate trait for a crate type may be implemented in any module of the crate), give pane_verbs.rs its own small private `fn tmux_call(args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String>` (Command::new("tmux"), stdin null, Err naming the argv), and make every tmux argv a PURE builder function (`fn send_text_argv(pane, text) -> Vec<Vec<String>>` returning the two calls, `fn rename_argv`, `fn list_panes_argv`, `fn tab_list_argv`, `fn tab_focus_argv`) plus a pure `fn parse_pane_rows(stdout: &str, session: Option<&str>) -> Vec<PaneRow>`; test the builders and the parser with no process (two calls with `-l` then `Enter`; `select-pane -T`; a 5-column tab-separated line; an empty title → label None).

truths: Every cockpit pane action the role docs need has a bee herding verb that works on both transports
The JSON envelope keys are identical across transports and pinned by tests
bee herding pane-id --label <l> returns the pane whose herdr label or tmux title equals <l>

trace.outcome: bee herding pane/agent-start/pane-id/result verbs run on both transports over a new CockpitTransport trait
deviations: CockpitTransport carries a 7th method pane_context() -> {pane_id, tab_id?, workspace_id?}: the cell requires pane current to render tab/workspace and tab-create to fall back to the caller workspace, and PaneTransport::pane_current returns only a pane id

pane layout renders {panes:[{pane_id,width,height}]} instead of the cell listed {} — role-dispatch reads layout to pick split geometry, so an empty result would make the verb unusable for its only caller
tmux pane listing uses list-panes -s (one session) instead of -a plus a client-side filter: the pinned 5-column format carries no session column, so parse_pane_rows drops the unused session parameter
run.rs RealHerdr::call and read_main_config widened to pub(crate) alongside RealHerdr itself, so pane_verbs reuses the one herdr spawn-and-decode helper instead of a second copy
pane read accepts and ignores herdr flag --source, so one role line reads the same on both transports
the D3 blocked-preflight reads TmuxSettings from a module OnceLock set by cockpit_transport_for, because RealTmux keeps its settings private and tmux.rs is owned by another cell
